records.text: A Skeletal Flayer is an undead combatant found in the Western Plaguelands. Commander Ashlam Valorfist identifies Skeletal Flayers among the undead haunting Sorrow Hill and assigns their removal as part of clearing the eastern approach to Andorhal. In combat, this flayer uses Thrash.
A Skeletal Sorcerer is an undead combatant found in the Western Plaguelands. Its fighting spells are Frostbolt and Fire Nova, marking it out among the skeletal enemies encountered in the region.
A Skeletal Terror is an undead combatant found in the Western Plaguelands. When badly wounded, it can cast Fear, making its response to injury a notable danger in a fight.
A Skeletal Executioner is an undead combatant found in the Western Plaguelands. It uses Cleave in combat, fitting the direct threat suggested by its executioner name.

A Skeletal Warlord is a scarce undead combatant found in the Western Plaguelands. Its combat technique is Mortal Strike, distinguishing this more powerful skeletal fighter from the region's other undead.
A Skeletal Acolyte is an undead combatant found in the Western Plaguelands. It casts Shadow Bolt in combat, giving this acolyte a ranged magical threat distinct from the skeletal fighters nearby.

A Slavering Ghoul is an undead creature found around Sorrow Hill in the Western Plaguelands. Commander Ashlam Valorfist includes the ghouls haunting Sorrow Hill among the targets to clear from the eastern approach to Andorhal. In combat, this ghoul uses Thrash.
A rotting ghoul encountered in the local area, this undead foe attacks with Contagion of Rot.
A soulless ghoul encountered in the local area, this undead foe attacks with Shadow Bolt Volley.
A searing ghoul encountered in the local area, this undead foe attacks with Flame Shock.
A freezing ghoul encountered in the local area, this undead foe attacks with Flash Freeze.
A hungering wraith encountered in the local area, this undead foe attacks with Debilitating Touch and can become enraged.
Wailing Death is an undead creature encountered in the local area; it attacks with Wailing Dead.
A flesh golem of the Western Plaguelands, this heavy undead creature strikes intruders with a knock-away attack.
A vile slime found in the Western Plaguelands, this hostile ooze can unleash a burst of crimson fury in combat.
A devouring ooze found across the Western Plaguelands, it can summon an oozeling when it dies.
A carrion vulture of the Western Plaguelands, this bird swoops at foes in combat.
A rotting behemoth roaming the Western Plaguelands, this creature releases a plague cloud in combat.
A decaying horror of the Western Plaguelands, this creature attacks with a hostile spell when roused.
A diseased black bear roaming the Western Plaguelands, it can infect its opponent with a wound when fighting.

A diseased grizzly suffering from the Scourge plague, its fur and flesh rot and its muscles stiffen. Mulgris Deepriver asks others to end the animals' misery; this grizzly is an objective in that plea, not its speaker.
A diseased wolf suffering from the Scourge plague, it is one of the animals Mulgris Deepriver asks others to put out of their misery. The wolf is the objective of his plea, not its speaker.
Carrion Lurkers are beasts of the Western Plaguelands. They attack with poison and can also ensnare a foe in a web.
Venom Mist Lurkers are beasts found in the Western Plaguelands. In combat they use a venomous attack.
Plague Lurkers are beasts of the Western Plaguelands. They use a plague attack during combat.

A Scarlet Mage serves the Scarlet Crusade, which vows to destroy those it sees as tainted by the Scourge and to drive evil from these lands. The mage threatens intruders with the Twisting Nether and casts fire in combat.

A Scarlet Sentinel serves the Scarlet Crusade, which vows to destroy those it sees as tainted by the Scourge and to drive evil from these lands. The sentinel threatens intruders with the Twisting Nether and uses overpowering force in combat.

A Scarlet Hunter serves the Scarlet Crusade, which vows to destroy those it sees as tainted by the Scourge and to drive evil from these lands. The hunter threatens intruders with the Twisting Nether and attacks with a ranged weapon.
A Scarlet spellcaster who brings fire magic to combat.
A Scarlet Crusade knight who denounces the Scourge’s taint and vows to destroy those it considers wicked. The knight’s battle cries speak for the Crusade.
A Scarlet Crusade paladin who denounces the Scourge’s taint and vows to destroy those it considers wicked. The paladin’s battle cries speak for the Crusade.
A Scarlet Crusade invoker who denounces the Scourge’s taint and vows to destroy those it considers wicked. The invoker’s battle cries speak for the Crusade.
A Scarlet cavalier, an elite combatant in the Scarlet forces.
An elite combatant bearing the title Scarlet Judge.
An elite humanoid called the Scarlet Interrogator, encountered in the Hearthglen area. When an aggressor draws it into a fight, it casts a spell.
The Scarlet High Clerist is an elite humanoid encountered in Hearthglen, distinguished by its clerical title.
An elite humanoid called the Scarlet Executioner, encountered in the Hearthglen area. It becomes enraged and uses an attack once a fight is underway.

Highlord Taelan Fordring leads the Scarlet Crusade at Hearthglen, yet his memories of his father and the life he once imagined remain painfully close. He recalls dreaming of joining the Order beside his father to fight the Scourge in service to the Alliance and Lordaeron, and says he has lived as a puppet of the Grand Crusader. If given the box, he can react with shock and mounting fury. He says he will lead the visitor through Hearthglen to the forest’s edge to be taken to his father, warns the disguised visitor to remove the disguise, and can call out to Isillien.
Foreman Jerris is an elite humanoid encountered in the Hearthglen area. He uses Thrash and responds to heavy injury with another attack.
Foreman Marcrid is a rare humanoid who uses multiple abilities in combat.
High Protector Tarsen is a humanoid High Protector in the Western Plaguelands.
High Protector Lorik is a humanoid High Protector in the Western Plaguelands.
Foulmane is a rare undead combatant whose fighting behavior includes several abilities.
Lord Maldazzar is a rare humanoid who uses an ability in combat.
Putridius fights as an undead creature and casts an ability in combat.
The Husk is a rare elemental.

Araj the Summoner is a lich who holds Andorhal from the ruined city’s center. He was formerly the leader of Scholomance and now commands a retinue of Scourge guardians; his phylactery and scarab are sought as proof of his destruction and as parts of a key to Scholomance.

High Priest Thel'danis guards Uther's Tomb and invokes the Light against those who threaten it. He purges evil from scourgestones for a plan to use righteous fire against the Scourge. Though he knows this cleansing can draw undead attention, he expresses confidence in allies' strength in the Light.
Scarlet Workers are laborers who use Head Crack in combat.
Scarlet Lumberjacks cut timber.
Scarlet Smiths work as smiths.
Haunting Visions are undead creatures.
Rotting Cadavers are decaying undead corpses.

A Scarlet Crusade avenger who sees the Scourge’s taint as a mark of the wicked. It warns that the Crusade will destroy those it judges tainted and promises to drive evil from the land, treating its violence as righteous punishment.

A Scarlet Crusade spellbinder whose Frostbolt serves its combat role. Like its fellow crusaders, it frames the fight as a righteous campaign: it calls its enemies tainted by the Scourge and vows that the Crusade will destroy the wicked and drive evil from these lands.

A Scarlet Medic serving the Crusade in its campaign against those it considers tainted by the Scourge. Its combat taunts promise the Crusade will destroy such enemies and drive evil from the land, presenting the faction’s violence as righteous. Its title marks a medical role.

A Scarlet Priest of the Crusade who condemns enemies as tainted by the Scourge. It speaks of the Crusade as an instrument for smiting the wicked and driving evil from the land, and warns that its foes will be destroyed. Its combat spell supports a priestly role.

Chromie, whose true name is Chronormu, is a bronze dragon attuned to time and its changing flow. In Andorhal's crisis, she works from another timeline to limit contamination while mending damage and opposing suspected Scourge tampering. She regards preserving the timeline as a duty of the bronze dragonflight, and sees mortals' present choices as shaping a changing future. Her familiarity with visitors reflects her temporal perspective; she chooses not to be overwhelmed by the sorrow of the places where she serves.

Mulgris Deepriver is a tauren druid who came to the Western Plaguelands to heal the damage the Scourge’s plague had done to nature. After catching the disease himself, he asked for diseased wolves and grizzlies to be put down as the only mercy left to them. As he was dying, he entrusted a glyph-marked oaken branch to carry his final message toward the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus.

Janice Felstone is a ghost on the Felstone Farm, still frightened by the plague and confused about what is happening around her. She anxiously asks for a package to be delivered and calls for her husband, John. The two halves of their good luck charm are tied to her hope that they can be together and safe; receiving the reassembled charm brings her clarity and releases her from that longing.
An infected deer, a critter.
A Wandering Skeleton is undead and can carry the Dalson Outhouse Key.

Commander Ashlam Valorfist leads the Alliance presence at Chillwind Camp, where Stormwind and its allies fight the Scourge. He organizes the advance toward Andorhal, directing efforts through Sorrow Hill and against the city's watchtowers. Valorfist describes Araj the Summoner as Andorhal's controlling lich and calls for allies to destroy him and bring back a shard of his phylactery as proof.

Officer Pureheart introduces himself as a proud Argent Dawn member, calling both Alliance and Horde allies in the fight against evil and rejecting a political role for the order. He directs commissioned fighters to bring Scourgestones for valor tokens, which can improve standing or serve as payment to quartermasters.

Quartermaster Lightspark identifies himself as an authorized Argent Dawn equipment and materiel officer. He explains that Officer Pureheart awards valor tokens, which quartermasters exchange for special goods, and presents access to the Dawn's magic-resistant mantles as a reward for service and standing.

Marlene Redpath is Pamela Redpath’s aunt and a wandering spirit of Darrowshire. She hid Pamela when the battle began, then lost track of her. Still grieving for her brother Joseph, whose soul the Scourge twisted into a monster, Marlene cannot bring herself to explain his fate to Pamela. She asks for help finding the child and for Joseph’s wedding ring to be taken to Chromie, hoping his fate might still be changed.

Jeziba, known as the Sculptor, shapes heroes through ordeals as well as forging armor. Their catalogue sets a dangerous trial chosen by Haleh, and they treat survival and its scars as the journey’s true reward. They fashion chromatic-flight armor from the creatures’ own remains, urging the wearer to turn their kin’s fear against them.

Weldon Barov is a proud, contemptuous noble of the House of Barov, locked in a bitter inheritance feud with his undead brother Alexi. He first sends an agent to recover the family deeds from Scholomance, then calls for Alexi’s assassination to secure his fortune and remove a threat to his own safety. He boasts of victory but panics when assassins arrive.

High Priestess MacDonnell coordinates the effort to sabotage the Scourge’s plague cauldrons in the Western Plaguelands, briefing agents and tracking the operation’s overall progress. She directs the work to turn the cauldrons’ plague against the Scourge, while Alchemist Arbington handles reports on the reagents each cauldron requires. She speaks with confidence in the Light and treats the campaign as a struggle against the Scourge.

Alchemist Arbington coordinates two distinct efforts at Chillwind Point: preparing the Western Plaguelands' Scourge cauldrons and constructing Scholomance's Skeleton Key. His cauldron work involves a vitreous focuser and unstable arcane quickener to identify and treat the needed Scourge components. For the key, he directs the collection of skeletal fragments, studies how to make a key that opens Scholomance, and uses a special solvent to bind Araj's scarab into the finished key. His dialogue shifts from practical instructions to expressed amazement at the hero's achievement.

Eva Sarkhoff is Lucien's wife and a lost soul of Caer Darrow. She directs visitors against the horrors tied to her death, connecting Krastinov's crimes to his master Kirtonos through Jandice Barov and the blood of innocents. After Kirtonos falls, she says Scholomance's grim story still has more chapters.

Caer Darrow's citizens are preparing for Uther Lightbringer's visit, and the rush can make them sound abrupt. Their greetings, praise for Baker Masterson, and affection for the island show everyday town pride beneath the bustle.

A Caer Darrow guardsman who warns visitors against causing trouble in town. His posted rules forbid loitering, panhandling, cursing, fighting, and other mischief, and his remarks show a short temper toward people he suspects of wrongdoing.
A cannoneer stationed at Caer Darrow, serving in the settlement's artillery role.

A mounted Caer Darrow guard who shares the town watch's stern warnings to visitors. The guards insist that loitering, panhandling, cursing, fighting, and other mischief are forbidden, and speak with suspicion toward apparent troublemakers.
Melia takes part in a children's footrace at Caer Darrow. She celebrates winning, invites a rematch, and gives the race its start.
Sammy is Melia's fellow runner in the children's race at Caer Darrow. He objects when he thinks the race was unfair.

Magistrate Marduke is investigating how to restore Ras Frostwhisper to mortal life. He sends others to seek a keepsake from Ras’s human years, have it attuned, then use it in a final confrontation. Marduke’s replies show both surprise at finding a keepsake and resolve to pursue the opportunity, despite the danger.
Baker Masterson is a baker who sells goods.
Joseph Dirte handles waste management and says the Barov house keeps him busy with its refuse. His conversation also reveals that he misses Brandy, a personal attachment he mentions with affection.

Alexia Ironknife is resting at Chillwind before heading to Hearthglen. She has heard that the Scarlet Crusade once employed a mage who tried to make powerful bows and guns, but she does not know whether he succeeded. She speculates that the Crusade may have killed him to hide the work or out of distrust of arcane magic.

Kirsta Deepshadow is a wounded scout sent to weaken the Scarlet Crusade's outlying forces and gauge Hearthglen's defenses. Still recovering and unable to continue alone, she recruits help against the Crusade's key figures outside town before attempting to infiltrate Hearthglen herself. She warns that the town is dangerous and that she cannot protect or brief anyone entering it.

Cavalier Durgen is one of the important Scarlet Crusade members supporting its forces outside Hearthglen, according to scout Kirsta Deepshadow. She names him as a target in her effort to weaken the Crusade before attempting her own infiltration of the town.

Huntsman Radley is one of the important Scarlet Crusade members supporting its forces outside Hearthglen, according to scout Kirsta Deepshadow. She names him as a target in her effort to weaken the Crusade before attempting her own infiltration of the town.

Nathaniel Dumah returned to Chillwind Camp to reclaim the Northridge Lumber Mill, which his father ran before the family fled during the last great war. He blames the Scarlet Crusade for taking the mill and exploiting war's victims. After force failed, he turned to sabotage, arranging to infest the mill with plague-resistant termites. He is fiercely hostile to the Crusade and sees its defeat as justice for his family.

Myranda is an illusionist whose magic takes concentration and power; her guises last only briefly and fail if the wearer travels too far. She can create disguises for entry into Hearthglen and to fool the black dragonflight’s gatekeeper. She says she was Tirion’s most trusted adviser while he was Lord of Mardenholde, and was banished after dissenting from the Silver Hand’s verdict. She recognizes Rexxar’s deliberately blank letter and says she owes the Warchief favors.
The Spectral Attendant is an undead combatant that uses magic in a fight. It casts when it draws an enemy’s attention, then casts again as it is wounded.

Artist Renfray painted a portrait of Tirion Fordring's family during one of their visits to Caer Darrow. Now a cursed spirit haunting the island's ruins, Renfray remembers the past and the painting's fate, unlike many spirits trapped in their last happy memory.

Lord Tirion Fordring is Taelan’s father and is associated with the Order of the Silver Hand. If Isillien murders Taelan, Tirion grieves, condemns Isillien’s lost honor and calls on the Light to help him fight. In the aftermath of that loss, he declares the Order reborn and takes his place as its Highlord.
A large hostile slime, it attacks when roused and lashes out with spells, unleashing further magic as it weakens.

Flint Shadowmore is an SI:7 operative assigned to investigate the missing agents and gather reconnaissance on the Blightcaller in the Eastern Plaguelands. He reacts with grief to signs that his colleagues have died; learning that Nathanos Marris is the Blightcaller leaves him shocked and struggling to accept the news.
Bibilfaz Featherwhistle is the Gryphon Master who handles flight requests. When threatened, he calls for the guards, and an enraged gryphon appears when he is attacked.
Leonard Porter supplies leatherworkers and can repair equipment; he also serves as a quest contact.

Elder Moonstrike speaks of the stars as beacons of hope and strength, and wonders whether the wise or fortunate can find earthly truths by looking to the heavens. His conversations also point visitors toward other named elders, including Darkcore, Graveborn and Highpeak.
Elder Meadowrun reflects on the stars as beacons of hope and strength for the coming ages. Visitors can ask him about other elders, and he connects the heavens with earthly mysteries.

Anchorite Truuen is a newcomer to Azeroth who has studied its heroes and reveres Uther Lightbringer. He seeks to return one of Uther's holy relics to the tomb and asks for company on the journey, warning that the Scourge may attack and be drawn to the Mark.
The Western Plaguelands Flame Warden welcomes visitors to honor its local flame and urges them to desecrate Horde festival fires, expressing the Alliance framing of the ceremony.
Frax Bucketdrop is a flight master who offers fast travel.

place_records.text: You are in the Western Plaguelands, a plague-scarred land in the Eastern Kingdoms, held in places by the Alliance and in others by no one. Chillwind Camp is an Alliance stronghold, while Caer Darrow and the Thondroril River belong to no side. Diseased grizzlies, plague lurkers and rotting behemoths roam the land, and Scarlet Crusade forces hold the town of Hearthglen.
You are in Hearthglen, a town in the Western Plaguelands held by the Scarlet Crusade. Scarlet paladins, sentinels and magi are the dangers within its streets.

You are in Northridge Lumber Camp, a logging camp in the Western Plaguelands. Kirsta Deepshadow, a wounded scout, is recovering here and seeks help against the Scarlet Crusade's leaders outside Hearthglen. A spirit healer is here too, and Scarlet lumberjacks and diseased wolves are the dangers.

You are in the Ruins of Andorhal, a town in the Western Plaguelands. Skeletal acolytes, searing ghouls and skeletal executioners roam the streets. Chromie, a bronze dragon, works here to mend the timeline she believes Scourge meddling has damaged, and temporal parasites infest the silos. Jeziba, the Sculptor, forges armor here.

You are in Uther's Tomb, a holy site in the Western Plaguelands. High Priest Thel'danis, an Alliance priest, guards it and purges evil from scourgestones to use against the Scourge. His cleansing can draw undead attention.

You are in Sorrow Hill, a hill in the Western Plaguelands. Marlene Redpath, a wandering spirit of Darrowshire, is still grieving here for her brother Joseph. Myranda the Hag, an illusionist, can disguise travelers for entry into Hearthglen, but her magic fails when the wearer goes too far. Slavering ghouls and skeletal flayers roam the hill.
You are in The Weeping Cave, a cave in the Western Plaguelands. Vile slimes, devouring oozes and plague lurkers haunt it, with diseased grizzlies and rotting behemoths as well.

You are in Felstone Field, a farm in the Western Plaguelands. Janice Felstone, a frightened ghost, still haunts the house and calls for her husband John. A cauldron of poison stands on the farm. Skeletal flayers, slavering ghouls and Scarlet medics roam the fields.

You are in Dalson's Tears, a place in the Western Plaguelands. Rotting cadavers, blighted zombies and skeletal terrors roam it, along with diseased wolves and carrion lurkers. A cauldron of ichors stands here.

You are in Gahrron's Withering, a place in the Western Plaguelands. Hungering wraiths, wailing deaths and haunting visions drift through it, with diseased grizzlies and plague lurkers as well. A cauldron of putrid ichors stands here.

You are in The Writhing Haunt, a place in the Western Plaguelands. Mulgris Deepriver, a tauren druid, came here to heal the land the plague damaged, and he caught the disease himself. Rotting and freezing ghouls, plague lurkers and diseased grizzlies are the dangers here.
You are in The Bulwark, a place in the Western Plaguelands. Diseased black bears, venom mist lurkers and carrion vultures roam it.

You are in Caer Darrow, an island town in the Western Plaguelands that no side holds. It has repairs, a spirit healer and goods for sale. Eva Sarkhoff, a lost soul, lingers here, and Magistrate Marduke seeks a way to restore the lich Ras Frostwhisper to mortal life. Town guards forbid loitering, panhandling and fighting.
You are in Thondroril River, a spot in Western Plaguelands. Frax Bucketdrop keeps the flight master's perch here and offers fast travel onward. Rotting behemoths and devouring oozes roam the area.

You are in Chillwind Camp, an Alliance camp in Western Plaguelands. Commander Ashlam Valorfist leads the Alliance here and organizes the advance toward Andorhal against the Scourge. High Priestess MacDonnell directs agents working to turn the plague cauldrons against the Scourge, and the camp has a flight master, repairs, a vendor and a spirit healer. Members of the Argent Dawn are here too.
